LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 5.3.1 SIMPLE PRESENT TENSE

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Language Use 5.3.1 Simple Present Tense
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 5.3.1 Simple Present Tense, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: What do you do everyday? - I wake up every day. - I go to school every day. What do you do from morning to evening?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 5.3.1 Simple Present Tense together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: The learner connects using technology as they use the internet and other social media sites to watch a video on routine activities and

talk about the activities.

• Communication: The learner’s ability to sign clearly and correctly is enhanced as they share about the activities they do every day.

Values:
Respect: accountability is nurtured as learners respond to questions based on daily routines.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: self-esteem is promoted as learners apply present tense forms to talk about time and sequence of routine or daily activities.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Learners relate the concept of simple present tense to the concept of activities taking place at different times of the day learnt in Environmental

Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Manual alphabet chart, flash cards, internet, posters, online dictionaries, assistive devices fitted with appropriate technologies such as hearing aids and

amplifiers, adapted course books, flash cards, sign language dictionary, internet, signed audio-visual recordings
